newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures rangebound in light volume.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures rangebound in light volume.

text.p: IPE Brent futures clung to earlier modest gains at midday on Monday, but volume was light in a directionless market, traders said.
January Brent was 10 cents higher at $23.13 a barrel at 1214 GMT, just under interim resistance at $23.17. December gas oil was $1.00 lower at $221.75 a tonne.

Jitters over when the U.N.-Iraqi oil-for-food deal would be implemented as well as concerns over product supply in Europe and the U.S. continued to hang over the market, but there was little to provide much immediate impetus.
"It's very quiet," one trader said. "A few people will be waiting to see what NYMEX does, but I'm not expecting a very busy week, given the U.S. holiday at the end of the week."
The U.S. celebrates Thanksgiving Day on Thursday and key markets including NYMEX will be shut on Thursday and Friday.
"The market's really products-led and until we see them moving one way or another Brent's going to stick in range," said another trader. "Wednesday could be pretty volatile, what with heat's expiry."
Traders said the market continued to monitor the outcome of the Cargill/AIC duel over the record IPE 865,100 tonne delivery into the November contract.

AIC, the predominant short, said last week that Cargill had failed to lift the required amount of material in the first delivery window spanning November 16-20 and that it was behind in its nominations for the second November 21-25 period.
Cargill, which has indicated it intends lifting 260,000 tonnes in the second period, declined to comment. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714
